title: Affine chart diagrams along an affine-transition limit
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set, $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and an $S_{i_0}$-morphism $g_0:U_0\to V_0$. Suppose given a finite affine open covering $V_0=\bigcup_jY_{j,0}$, affine opens $W_{j,0}\subseteq S_{i_0}$ containing the image of $Y_{j,0}$, and finite affine open coverings $g_0^{-1}(Y_{j,0})=\bigcup_kX_{jk,0}$. Write $W_{j,0}=\operatorname{Spec}R^{(j)}_0$, $Y_{j,0}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{j,0}$ and $X_{jk,0}=\operatorname{Spec}C_{jk,0}$, and write $\varphi_{jk,0}:B_{j,0}\to C_{jk,0}$ for the induced $R^{(j)}_0$-algebra map [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $p_i:S_i\to S_{i_0}$ for $i\geq i_0$ and $p:S\to S_{i_0}$ be the given projections. Then $p_i^{-1}(W_{j,0})=\operatorname{Spec}R^{(j)}_i$ and $p^{-1}(W_{j,0})=\operatorname{Spec}R^{(j)}$ are affine, with $R^{(j)}=\varinjlim_{i\geq i_0}R^{(j)}_i$ compatibly with all projections. For $T=S_i$ or $T=S$, put $A_j=R^{(j)}_i$ or $R^{(j)}$, respectively. In the base changes $U_T,V_T,g_T$ to $T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the inverse images $X_{jk,T}$ and $Y_{j,T}$ of the given opens form affine open coverings, and their identifications with $\operatorname{Spec}(A_j\otimes_{R^{(j)}_0}C_{jk,0})$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(A_j\otimes_{R^{(j)}_0}B_{j,0})$ identify $g_T|_{X_{jk,T}}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi_{jk,0})$. These identifications commute with both projections and with the transition maps. In particular, for $i_0\leq i'\leq i$, the square with horizontal maps $X_{jk,i}\to Y_{j,i}$ and $X_{jk,i'}\to Y_{j,i'}$ and vertical transition maps is cartesian. Writing $R_\bullet=R^{(j)}_\bullet$, $B_0=B_{j,0}$ and $C_0=C_{jk,0}$, its coordinate comparison is the canonical isomorphism $(R_{i'}\otimes_{R_0}C_0)\otimes_{R_{i'}\otimes_{R_0}B_0}(R_i\otimes_{R_0}B_0)\cong C_0\otimes_{B_0}(R_i\otimes_{R_0}B_0)\cong R_i\otimes_{R_0}C_0$ as algebras over $R_i\otimes_{R_0}B_0$.

The pulled-back chart systems, their affine colimit rings and the natural tensor-product comparison, including the stage-change square (old proof step 2 and the tensor comparison in old step 3).

proof.text: Fix $j$ and work on the upper tail $J=\{i\mid i\geq i_0\}$, a nonempty directed set: a common upper bound in $I$ of two elements of $J$ is again in $J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] the projections to $S_{i_0}$ are affine and the inverse images $W_{j,i}$ of $W_{j,0}$ have limit $W_j=p^{-1}(W_{j,0})$, with the specified restricted projections. By [pqf-def-affine-morphism], all these inverse images are affine. Put $R_i^{(j)}=\Gamma(W_{j,i},\mathcal O)$ and use the pullbacks of sections for their directed transition homomorphisms. The affine clause of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], applied to this restricted system, gives $W_j\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_J R_i^{(j)})$. To fix the projections: by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], $\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_J R_i^{(j)})$ with the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the coprojections is a limit of the same system $(W_{j,i})_{i\in J}$ in schemes, so the unique isomorphism of limits compatible with the projections identifies $W_j$ with it; under this identification each restricted projection $W_j\to W_{j,i}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the coprojection $R_i^{(j)}\to\varinjlim_J R_i^{(j)}$. Use the given identification $W_{j,0}=\operatorname{Spec}R_0^{(j)}$ to transport the ring at $i_0$ to $R_0^{(j)}$; [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies its global sections with that ring. Thus these are $R_0^{(j)}$-algebras and the limit comparison respects all their structure maps. No quasi-compactness of $S_i$ is needed.

Write $T_j=T\times_{S_{i_0}}W_{j,0}$ for either allowed $T$; step 1 identifies it with $\operatorname{Spec}A_j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to the opens $Y_{j,0}\subset V_0$, $W_{j,0}\subset S_{i_0}$ and $T_j\subset T$. Since $Y_{j,0}$ maps into $W_{j,0}$, its inverse image in $V_T$ is $Y_{j,0}\times_{W_{j,0}}T_j$, with both projections unchanged. The same argument applies to $X_{jk,0}\subset U_0$ since its image lies in $Y_{j,0}$, hence in $W_{j,0}$. These opens cover: every point of $V_T$ projects into some $Y_{j,0}$, and every point of $U_T$ projects into $g_0^{-1}(Y_{j,0})$ for some $j$, then into some $X_{jk,0}$. For fixed $j$, the $X_{jk,T}$ cover $g_T^{-1}(Y_{j,T})$ by the same preimage-of-union argument. All index sets remain the given finite ones.

source.place: Tag 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product); Limits Tag 0C4W (lemma-descend-unramified), proof, affine-cover reduction

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the products in step 2 are affine with rings $A_j\otimes_{R_0^{(j)}}B_{j,0}$ and $A_j\otimes_{R_0^{(j)}}C_{jk,0}$. Their projection homomorphisms send $a$ to $a\otimes1$ and $b$ (respectively $c$) to $1\otimes b$ (respectively $1\otimes c$). The restricted $g_T$ commutes with these projections, so its ring homomorphism must send $a\otimes b$ to $a\otimes\varphi_{jk,0}(b)$. This determines it because pure tensors additively generate the tensor product. By the contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the restricted morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi_{jk,0})$. For a transition ring map $\alpha:A_j\to A'_j$, including a map to the colimit ring, the two chart transition homomorphisms are $a\otimes b\mapsto\alpha(a)\otimes b$ and $a\otimes c\mapsto\alpha(a)\otimes c$: their restrictions to each factor are the required projection maps, which uniquely determine the homomorphisms. The two paths in each square both send $a\otimes b$ to $\alpha(a)\otimes\varphi_{jk,0}(b)$. This proves compatibility with projections and every transition, including identity and composite transitions.

For $i_0\leq i'\leq i$, consider the three rows $(X_{jk,i},X_{jk,i'})$, $(Y_{j,i},Y_{j,i'})$, $(W_{j,i},W_{j,i'})$, with horizontal transition maps and vertical structure maps. Step 2 identifies each chart with its original chart pulled back to $W_{j,i}$ or $W_{j,i'}$. Pullback pasting [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] therefore makes both the lower square (the $Y$ row over the $W$ row) and the outer rectangle (the $X$ row over the $W$ row) cartesian: each is obtained by pasting the defining pullback squares over $W_{j,0}$ and cancelling their common right square. Apply that same pasting statement once more to cancel the lower square. The upper square is cartesian. Transposing this square gives exactly the square with horizontal maps $X_{jk,i}\to Y_{j,i}$ and $X_{jk,i'}\to Y_{j,i'}$ in the statement.

For the coordinate comparison abbreviate $A=R_{i'}$, $A'=R_i$, $D=A\otimes_{R_0}B_0$, $E=A'\otimes_{R_0}B_0$, and write $\alpha:A\to A'$ for the transition. Here $D\to A\otimes C_0$ sends $a\otimes b$ to $a\otimes\varphi(b)$ and $D\to E$ sends it to $\alpha(a)\otimes b$. Define
$$F:(A\otimes C_0)\otimes_D E\longrightarrow C_0\otimes_{B_0}E,\qquad (a\otimes c)\otimes(a'\otimes b)\longmapsto c\otimes(\alpha(a)a'\otimes b).$$
Its inverse sends $c\otimes e$ to $(1\otimes c)\otimes e$. The $R_0$-balancing follows from the structure maps, and the $D$-balancing follows by moving $a_1\otimes b_1$ between the two factors: both images are $c\otimes(\alpha(a_1a)a'\otimes b_1b)$, using $\varphi(b_1)c\otimes e=c\otimes(1\otimes b_1)e$ on the target. The same identity proves the inverse is $B_0$-balanced. Both maps are additive, multiplicative and preserve the unit; they fix $E$ under its second-factor action. Their composites fix pure tensors: in the source move $a\otimes1\in D$ from the first factor to the second; in the target the assertion is immediate. Thus $F$ is the first asserted $E$-algebra isomorphism. This is an explicit verification from the defining balanced tensor relations, not an additional lemma.

The second isomorphism is $G:C_0\otimes_{B_0}E\to A'\otimes_{R_0}C_0$, $c\otimes(a'\otimes b)\mapsto a'\otimes\varphi(b)c$, with inverse $a'\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes(a'\otimes1)$. The $B_0$-balancing is precisely $\varphi(b)c\otimes e=c\otimes(1\otimes b)e$; $R_0$-balancing uses that $\varphi$ is an $R_0$-algebra map. These relations also show both composites are identities. The maps preserve addition, multiplication, unit and the $E$-action, where $a'\otimes b$ acts on the target as $a'\otimes\varphi(b)$. Finally $GF$ sends $(a\otimes c)\otimes(a'\otimes b)$ to $\alpha(a)a'\otimes c\varphi(b)$. This is the coordinate map of the cartesian square of step 4: it extends its two ring maps $a\otimes c\mapsto\alpha(a)\otimes c$ and $a'\otimes b\mapsto a'\otimes\varphi(b)$. Uniqueness in the tensor-product universal property identifies it with the canonical comparison. This also verifies the specified algebra structure, rather than only an abstract ring isomorphism.
